# MPkWh.com

> MPkWh.com ranks the most efficient electric cars available in the US by miles per kWh (Mi/kWh) — the EV equivalent of MPG. Data is sourced from official EPA fuel economy ratings and updated weekly every Monday.

## What is Mi/kWh?

Miles per kilowatt-hour (Mi/kWh) measures how far an electric vehicle travels on one unit of electricity. A higher number means greater efficiency: lower energy consumption, lower running costs, and longer range from the same battery. Mi/kWh is calculated as EPA-rated range divided by usable battery capacity — the portion of the pack the car can actually access. This measures battery-to-wheel efficiency.

## Notes

- Mi/kWh = EPA range ÷ usable battery capacity. Measures battery-to-wheel efficiency (not wall-to-wheel, which would include charging losses).
- Efficiency figures reflect the most efficient trim and configuration available for each model year.
- Pack sizes sourced from ev-database.org, manufacturer spec pages, and EPA energy calculations (range × kWh/100mi × 0.89 charging efficiency). Tesla does not publicly disclose battery capacity — Tesla usable kWh figures are cross-verified via EPA energy data and C&D spec boxes.
- Not all 2026 models have received EPA ratings yet. The table is updated every Monday as new ratings are published.
- Cost-per-100-miles uses the latest US average residential electricity rate published monthly by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA). As of July 2026: $0.1844/kWh (May 2026 figure, published July 2026).
- Data source: US EPA fueleconomy.gov, ev-database.org
